items.heading: ## 5. Pattern: Implementing a Custom Data Type
items.text: The `AsmModel` service carries `name=<model name>` instead, so its `@Reference` target is `(name=<app>)`. The code sample below must use `(name=YourApplicationName)` for the `AsmModel` reference.

items.heading: #### Accessing the Logged-in User in Java
items.text: 1.  Inject the `hu.blackbelt.judo.dispatcher.api.VariableResolver` service using `@Reference`. The service is registered once per model with `judo.model.name=<model name>`; add `target = "(judo.model.name=<app>)"` to the `@Reference` when the runtime hosts more than one model.

items.heading: ### Decision cheat sheet
items.text: An `OperationForm` may sit directly in a view. The validation rule `ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition` requires the view to be the page container of the operation's owning transfer object (or of its action definition); it does not require an `ActionGroup`.

items.heading: ## 10. Operations wiring
items.text: A UI child that has no position in its ESM container's `components` list stops the generator with `Missing position parameter(s)`. Place every widget in the ESM with `move <fqn> --index n` before generation, so the widget takes its position in the sorted children.

items.heading: Constraints
items.text: The primary link is an association and cascades nothing: deleting the primary contact clears the parent's primary link and leaves the parent in place. The link is optional (0..1) and has no reverse cascade delete, so the contact delete is not refused.
items.replaces: The primary link is an association and cascades nothing.

items.heading: Frontend guidance
items.text: A list call returns only a count when the request sends a non-blank `X-Judo-CountRecords` header. A row action is hidden per row with the button's hidden condition; the generated table evaluates it for each row.

items.heading: Pattern 3: Manual Transaction Control
items.text: `JudoRuntimeFixture.tearDown()` only rolls back a transaction that is still open. It does not close the injector or the datasource, so close the datasource yourself (for example in `@AfterEach`) when a test manages its own datasource.

items.heading: `judo.sh build` flag reference
items.text: `-KA` (skip Karaf) does not rebuild the `karaf-offline` package. `./judo.sh start` re-extracts that package on every start, so `build -F -KA` after Java changes leaves the running backend on the old custom operations. Drop `-KA` (or run `build -M -F`) before `start`.
